subject: Ops log delivery and custody — SIG / SOC2 clarifications
messages:
From: Marta Sanchez <marta.sanchez@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ops log delivery & custody — SIG/SOC2 clarifications

Hi Kimberly,

We are preparing materials for our SIG and SOC2 assessment and need to confirm the scope and delivery options for Redwood's admin/ops logs. The auditor is specifically asking for: what is captured (admin actions, role changes, API key usage, model version pinning, dataset access, privileged sessions), default retention, encryption-at-rest/in-transit, redaction options for PII, and export formats and chain-of-custody proof (manifest, checksums, signatures).

Can you provide a concise summary we can hand to the auditor, plus your preferred export methods (SFTP, signed HTTPS download, or shipping an attested bundle)? We attached the current SIG/SOC2 questionnaire — please populate the relevant sections or point us to the right artifacts.

Attachment: SIG_SOC2_questionnaire_v2.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Marta Sanchez
Compliance Manager
Greenline Health
marta.sanchez@greenlinehealth.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Ops log delivery & custody — SIG/SOC2 clarifications

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; we can produce an attested bundle and a manifest for your auditor.

What we log (admin / operator actions) — typical entries include:
- User lifecycle: create/update/delete admin users, role/permission changes, MFA changes
- Authentication events: successful/failed console/API auth attempts (IP, user agent)
- Privileged operations: model pinning/version rollouts, model promotion/demotion, serving config changes
- Key management: API key creation/revocation, KMS-handoff events (no secret material attached)
- Tenant and data access: dataset access events, data export triggers, storage/object reads by ops tools
- System ops: scaling, instance replacement, agent upgrades tied to operator identity

Retention & storage
- Hosted default retention: 365 days for admin activity by default; shorter windows (90d) are available on request for dedicated/private deployments and can be set per-contract.
- Data-at-rest encrypted with customer-aware KMS keys; in transit over TLS 1.2+/mTLS for internal replication.

Export & chain-of-custody options
- Export formats: JSONL (line-delimited events), Parquet (columnar bulk), CSV for summary exports.
- Delivery modes: secure SFTP (preferred for large bundles), pre-authorized S3 signed URLs (expiring), or HTTPS push to your collector.
- Manifest: we create a signed manifest (SHA256 checksums per file + overall fingerprint) and can PGP- or KMS-sign the manifest for attestation.
- Proof: manifest includes checksum, timestamp, delivery method, and operator who requested export. We can provide an audit email trail and HMAC verification on the manifest.

Redaction & PII handling
- PII in logs (user email, IP) can be pseudonymized or hashed at export time; we maintain raw material for the retention window internally and provide scrubbed exports on request. Redaction policy is recorded in the manifest.

Next steps
1) Tell us your preferred delivery method (SFTP vs S3 signed URL) and desired retention window for the evidence bundle.
2) We will produce a sample snapshot and manifest for your auditor to validate.

Attachment: admin-activity-manifest.template.xlsx (xlsx) — template for manifest fields we populate.

If useful, Logan can include the exact schema and a short sample export.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Ops log delivery & custody — SIG/SOC2 clarifications

Kim / Marissa — following up with technical specifics to include in the sample. Quoting Kimberly below for context: 

On Sat, May 9, 2026 at 11:40 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> We can create a signed manifest (SHA256 checksums per file + overall fingerprint) and can PGP- or KMS-sign the manifest for attestation.

Notes to populate the manifest and sample payload: 
- Event schema (high level): timestamp (ISO8601), tenant_id, actor_id (hashed option), action_type, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, client_ip (hashable), user_agent, request_payload_ref (blob id), outcome (success/fail), severity.
- Snapshots: we support full-snapshot exports (timebox) and incremental deltas (cursor based). For auditors, full snapshots with manifest are easiest.
- Throughput & packaging: we produce gzipped JSONL files split by day or 10M events, whichever is smaller. Each file will have a SHA256 checksum; manifest contains file-level and bundle-level checksums.
- Signing: we offer two options — PGP-signed manifest or manifest signed using a Redwood attest key with an accompanying certificate chain. We can provide both if needed.
- Redaction proof: include a redaction map in the bundle (fields redacted, hashing algorithm, salt reference). The map itself is part of the signed manifest.
- Retention by deployment: hosted (default 365d), dedicated (configurable per contract; retention can be >= 30d), private on-prem (customer-managed). Mention this in the SIG response.

Attachment: sample-manifest.jsonl (jsonl) — small example we can hand to auditor.

I recommend we offer SFTP for initial handoff and S3 signed URLs for follow-up.

— Logan
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com

From: Marta Sanchez <marta.sanchez@greenlinehealth.com>

Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ops log delivery & custody — SIG/SOC2 clarifications

Kim — this is very helpful, thanks. A couple of follow-ups from our auditor and security team: 

- They want explicit confirmation that file-level SHA256 checksums will be provided and included in the manifest.
- We need PGP-signed manifest files (auditor mandate) and an independent time-stamp (RFC 3161) on the manifest if possible.
- For redaction, auditor requests a small attestation demonstrating the redaction map for a non-production tenant (to validate hashing algorithm).
- Please confirm SLA expectations: can you commit to delivering the attested snapshot within 7 business days after request? We may elevate to a formal request via our procurement team.

If you can confirm these items and send the sample manifest, we'll circulate to the SOC2 auditor and provide guidance on the preferred transfer mechanism (SFTP endpoint forthcoming).

Thanks again — copying our security alias.

Regards,
Marta

Marta — confirmed. Summary and next steps below.

Confirmations
- File-level SHA256 checksums: yes — every export file will include a SHA256 checksum in the signed manifest.
- PGP-signed manifest: yes — we will produce a PGP-signed manifest and can additionally sign with our attestation key.
- RFC3161 timestamp: we can obtain an RFC3161 timestamping service stamp for the manifest as part of the bundle.
- Redaction attestation: we will generate a scrubbed sample from a non-production tenant and include the redaction map (algorithm + salt reference) in the signed bundle.
- SLA: we can commit to 7 business days for initial attested snapshot delivery for hosted customers; if Greenline requires a contractual SLA for future requests, we can: a) include a one-off expedited request clause, or b) add a delivery SLA in a Dedicated/Private contract.

Proposed handoff plan (once Greenline provides SFTP endpoint or S3 bucket):
1) We prepare a full snapshot of the requested window and generate gzipped JSONL files split by day.
2) Generate manifest with per-file SHA256 checksums + bundle fingerprint; PGP-sign and obtain RFC3161 timestamp.
3) Upload to SFTP (or provide signed S3 URLs) and email manifest + verification instructions to your security alias.
4) If requested, we will provide a short attestation letter from Redwood Legal confirming chain-of-custody steps for the snapshot.

Attachment: delivery-sla-ack.txt (txt) — brief acknowledgement of 7 business day delivery for this request.

Please confirm preferred delivery mechanism and provide an endpoint. Once we have that, Logan will kick off the export and we’ll send the sample manifest for your auditor.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
